title: APHRC Virtual Learning Academy | Free Online Courses for African Researchers
summary: The African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC) has developed the APHRC Virtual Learning Academy (VLA) , an online learning platform offering flexible and accessible courses designed to strengthen research capacity and support evidence generation and uptake across Africa. The academy provides learning opportunities in areas including research and grant writing, data science, data governance, policy and advocacy, gender, grant management, artificial intelligence, and research capacity strengthening . Many of the courses currently listed on the platform are available free of charge , making the academy a useful resource for researchers, academics, professionals, and others looking to develop relevant skills. What Is the APHRC Virtual Learning Academy? The APHRC Virtual Learning Academy is designed to provide flexible, high-quality online learning focused particularly on the needs of African researchers. Learners can explore courses according to their study or research interests or based on their current or anticipated career roles . The academy covers several areas of professional and research development, including: Research and grantmanship Data Science Data Governance and Management Policy and Advocacy Gender Grant Management E-Learning Course Development Capacity Strengthening for Researchers Artificial Intelligence APHRC Training Programmes Free Online Courses Available The platform currently features a range of courses listed at 0.00 , providing learners with opportunities to develop practical skills without a course fee. Research and Grant Writing Researchers can access courses focused on grant proposal development, scientific writing, research visibility, data collection, and grant management. Examples include: Online Research Grant Writing Training for Early and Mid-Career Researchers in Africa Scientific Writing Course Grant Management Online Grant Writing Course for Early and Mid-Career Researchers Data Collection Training Course for Researchers Several research grant-writing courses are available in different tracks, including options for pre-PhD and PhD holders . Data Science and Data Governance The academy also offers learning opportunities related to data and digital research. Courses include Agent Based Modelling , as well as courses covering: Data Anonymization Data Quality Assurance Data Documentation Data Governance Data Access and Sharing Data Privacy and Protection Policy and Advocacy Learners interested in policy engagement can explore courses such as Policy Communication for Youth Leaders and Evidence-Informed Decision Making for Policy Actors in Sexual and Reproductive Health . The academy also provides courses on the visibility and discoverability of African journals and website strategy. Gender and Human Rights The platform includes learning opportunities related to gender and human rights, including Gender Transformative Programming and Human Rights and African Human Rights Mechanisms . Certificates and Learner Support The APHRC Virtual Learning Academy states that learners can obtain a verified certificate for every course they complete during their selected subscription period. The platform also highlights recognised certifications in areas including Data Science, Population Dynamics and Reproductive Health, Health and Wellbeing, and Human Development . Learners can also access a community of practice where they can continue discussions, share insights, and engage with peers. A dedicated support team consisting of facilitators, instructional designers, and multimedia specialists is available to support learners throughout their learning journey. Who Can Benefit From the Academy? The courses may be particularly useful for: African researchers Early-career researchers Mid-career researchers Academics and research professionals Policy and advocacy professionals Youth leaders Professionals interested in data and digital systems Individuals seeking to strengthen research and grant-writing skills The academy specifically describes its learning offer as focused on the needs of African researchers . How to Access the Courses Interested learners can visit the APHRC Virtual Learning Academy, create an account, and explore the available courses according to their interests and career goals. Apply / Enrol Visit the APHRC Virtual Learning Academy: https://soma.aphrc.org/home Register: https://soma.aphrc.org/register Conclusion The APHRC Virtual Learning Academy provides a wide range of online learning opportunities for people interested in strengthening their research, data, grant-writing, policy, and professional development skills. With numerous courses listed as free of charge and learning areas specifically focused on African research needs, the platform can be a valuable resource for researchers and professionals seeking to expand their knowledge and capabilities. Interested learners are encouraged to explore the available courses and select those that align with their academic, research, or career goals. title: EU Award for Gender Equality Champions 2026 | €400,000 Prize for Research and Innovation Organisations
summary: The European Commission has opened applications for the 2026 EU Award for Gender Equality Champions , recognising organisations that are driving meaningful and lasting change in gender equality across the European research and innovation sector. For the first time, organisations active in research and innovation from EU candidate countries are also eligible to apply, expanding the award’s reach beyond EU Member States and Associated Countries. With a total prize value of €400,000 , the award provides an opportunity for universities, higher education institutions, and research and innovation organisations to gain recognition for their efforts to advance institutional gender equality. About the EU Award for Gender Equality Champions Established in 2022 by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Research and Innovation, the award aims to encourage institutional and cultural change in gender equality across the European Research Area and beyond. The 2026 edition features three award categories, each recognising a different approach to advancing gender equality. Eligible organisations can apply to only one category . Award Categories 1. Sustainable Gender Equality Champions This category recognises organisations with a strong, long-term record of achieving structural change through the implementation of their Gender Equality Plans (GEPs) . Number of winners: 1 2. Newcomer Gender Equality Champions This category celebrates institutions that have recently completed their first Gender Equality Plan and can demonstrate significant progress in putting the plan into practice. Number of winners: 2 3. Inclusive Gender Equality Champions This category recognises pioneering institutions that address gender equality together with at least two other social categories , including racial or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, or social origin. Number of winners: 1 Who Can Apply? The award is open to eligible: Higher education institutions Universities Research organisations Organisations conducting research and innovation Eligible organisations must be based in EU Member States, Associated Countries, or countries currently holding EU candidate status , according to the applicable rules of the contest. Past winners of the award are not eligible to re-enter, and each organisation may submit an application to only one award category. Applicants should carefully review the official Rules of Contest and eligibility requirements before submitting their application. Prize The 2026 EU Award for Gender Equality Champions has a total prize value of €400,000 . The awards are designed not only to recognise institutional achievements but also to support the continued development of gender equality initiatives within successful organisations. Application Deadline The deadline to apply is: 29 September 2026 Applications must be submitted electronically through the EU Funding and Tenders Portal . Following the deadline, an independent jury of international experts will assess the applications. The winners are expected to be announced and celebrated at a dedicated award ceremony in Brussels in 2027 . How to Apply Eligible organisations should prepare their application according to the requirements outlined in the Rules of Contest and submit it online through the EU Funding and Tenders Portal before the deadline. Application Deadline: 29 September 2026 Prize Fund: €400,000 Application Platform: EU Funding and Tenders Portal Eligible Applicants: Universities, higher education institutions, research organisations and other eligible research and innovation organisations Apply Here EU Funding and Tenders Portal: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/ Official EU Award for Gender Equality Champions: https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/prizes/eu-award-gender-equality-champions_en Why This Award Matters Gender equality remains an important part of building a more inclusive and effective European research and innovation system. Through the EU Award for Gender Equality Champions, the European Commission is recognising institutions that are moving beyond policies on paper and demonstrating meaningful institutional change. The expansion of eligibility to EU candidate countries also creates an opportunity for more organisations across Europe to showcase innovative approaches to gender equality and contribute to a more inclusive European scientific community. Conclusion The 2026 EU Award for Gender Equality Champions offers eligible research and innovation organisations an opportunity to gain international recognition for their work in advancing gender equality. With €400,000 in prize funding and three distinct award categories, institutions that have demonstrated sustainable, innovative, or inclusive approaches to gender equality are encouraged to review the eligibility requirements and submit their applications before 29 September 2026 . title: Texas Aerospace Scholars Research Brief Development Opportunity at NASA Johnson Space Center: Apply for the Spring 2027 Program
summary: Are you a university student with strong writing, communication, research, education, engineering, science, or STEM interests and a passion for space exploration? NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC) is offering an opportunity to contribute to the Texas Aerospace Scholars (TAS) program through research, educational content development, and NASA-focused projects connected to the agency’s Moon-to-Mars exploration objectives. The Texas Aerospace Scholars – Research Brief Development position is designed for students who want to gain practical experience in a professional NASA environment while helping develop educational resources for high school students interested in aerospace, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Based at NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, the position involves developing research briefs, educational materials, newsletters, digital content, and other resources that translate complex NASA initiatives into engaging and accessible learning experiences. The program is scheduled for the Spring 2027 session, with registration opening on June 12, 2026, and closing on September 14, 2026. About the Texas Aerospace Scholars Opportunity The Texas Aerospace Scholars program is connected to NASA’s broader efforts to engage students in STEM education and inspire the next generation of aerospace professionals. The Research Brief Development position provides an opportunity for a student intern to support the development of educational and research content for TAS participants. A major focus of the assignment will be NASA’s Moon-to-Mars exploration objectives and how these objectives can be transformed into meaningful research projects for high school students. The selected student will work alongside TAS mentors and subject matter experts at NASA Johnson Space Center to research, write, edit, design, and develop educational resources. Rather than simply observing NASA operations, the student will be expected to make tangible contributions to the TAS program through the creation of professional-quality educational materials. NASA describes its internships as educational, hands-on experiences that provide participants with opportunities to gain NASA-related research and operational experience. For broader information about NASA internships, applicants can visit NASA Internships . What Will the Selected Student Work On? One of the central responsibilities of the position will be the development of comprehensive research briefs for Texas Aerospace Scholars students. The intern is expected to develop approximately 5–7 two-page research briefs aligned with NASA’s Moon-to-Mars exploration objectives. These research briefs are expected to contain several important components, including: Detailed descriptions of research projects. Scientific and technical background information. Exploratory activities designed for high school students. Clearly defined learning outcomes. Professionally formatted educational content suitable for distribution during TAS program sessions. Information that connects NASA exploration objectives with practical student research activities. The work therefore combines research, writing, editing, education, communication, STEM knowledge, and content development. Key Responsibilities The selected participant will undertake a broad range of communications, research, education, and content-development responsibilities. 1. Develop Educational Content The intern will research and create educational materials that help Texas Aerospace Scholars students understand complex aerospace and STEM concepts. This requires the ability to take technical information and transform it into content that is clear, engaging, accurate, and appropriate for a high school audience. 2. Prepare Research Briefs A major responsibility will be developing the 5–7 research briefs associated with the TAS program. The briefs will connect student research activities with NASA’s Moon-to-Mars exploration goals and provide students with structured opportunities to investigate relevant topics. 3. Research NASA Moon-to-Mars Initiatives The intern will research NASA initiatives associated with human exploration and the Moon-to-Mars pathway. This may require reviewing technical and scientific information and identifying the most relevant material for educational use. 4. Write and Edit TAS Materials The position involves writing content for a variety of Texas Aerospace Scholars communication and educational materials. This includes content for: TAS educational resources. Newsletters. Digital platforms. Research materials. Student-facing resources. Other program communications. 5. Translate Complex Information for Students An important part of the role is making complex technical concepts understandable to high school audiences. The successful applicant should therefore be able to communicate scientific and technical information without unnecessarily complicated language while maintaining accuracy. 6. Support TAS Engagement Events The intern will also support Texas Aerospace Scholars engagement activities and events. This may involve helping prepare materials, supporting educational activities, assisting with program logistics, or contributing to other initiatives connected to student engagement. 7. Collaborate With Mentors and Subject Matter Experts The position provides an opportunity to work with TAS mentors and subject matter experts at Johnson Space Center. Collaboration will be important because the intern will need to gather information, receive feedback, refine content, and ensure that educational materials meet program expectations. 8. Contribute to Special Projects In addition to the primary research-brief assignment, the intern may assist with special projects related to the Texas Aerospace Scholars program. This makes adaptability and the ability to manage multiple assignments particularly important. Work Schedule and Location The opportunity is an in-person, full-time position at NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas . The stated working schedule is: Location: Houston, Texas NASA Center: Johnson Space Center Format: In-person Schedule: Full-time Working hours: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Hours per week: 40 hours Session: Spring 2027 Because the position is fully on-site, applicants should be prepared to participate in the program physically at Johnson Space Center rather than remotely. Skills NASA Is Looking For The opportunity is particularly suitable for students who can combine strong communication skills with research, analytical, technical, educational, or STEM capabilities. The listing highlights several desired skills. Strong Writing, Editing and Proofreading The ability to write clearly and professionally is central to the position. Applicants should be comfortable researching information, drafting content, editing their own work, proofreading documents, and producing polished materials for students and program stakeholders. Ability to Work in a Fast-Paced Environment The position may involve several assignments and changing priorities. Applicants should therefore be capable of adapting quickly while maintaining accuracy and quality. Multi-Project Management The selected intern may have to work on multiple research briefs, educational resources, communications materials, and special projects simultaneously. Strong organizational and time-management abilities will therefore be valuable. Graphic Design Experience with graphic design for print and digital platforms is listed among the desired skills. Applicants who can combine writing with visual communication may be particularly well suited to the role. Communication Excellent communication skills will be important when working with mentors, subject matter experts, colleagues, and students. Teamwork The position requires collaboration across different areas, making the ability to work effectively as part of a team important. Problem Solving and Critical Thinking Applicants should be able to analyze information, identify challenges, develop solutions, and make sound decisions when preparing educational and research materials. Microsoft Office 365 Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 is among the desired technical skills. Canvas Learning Management Platform Familiarity with the Canvas learning management system is also identified as a desirable skill. Applicants who have previously used Canvas for educational, academic, or training purposes may find this experience particularly relevant. Ability to Translate Technical Content The ability to translate complex technical or scientific information into content suitable for educational audiences is particularly important. This is one of the defining aspects of the position because the research briefs are intended for high school students. NASA Mission or STEM Education Familiarity Familiarity with NASA missions or STEM education is preferred. While this is described as a preferred area rather than the sole basis for eligibility, applicants who understand NASA’s mission, aerospace exploration, STEM education, or Moon-to-Mars objectives may be better positioned to demonstrate their suitability. Academic Fields Relevant to the Opportunity The opportunity is open to students from a wide range of academic backgrounds. The listed preferred majors cover communications, education, engineering, engineering technologies, and physical sciences. Relevant academic areas include: Communication and Journalism Students studying communication, media studies, journalism, public information, or related communication fields may find the position especially relevant because of its strong writing, editing, research, and educational-content requirements. Education Relevant education fields include: Curriculum and instruction. General education. Educational assessment, evaluation, and research. Educational and instructional technology. Technology teacher education. Industrial arts teacher education. Engineering The listing includes an extensive range of engineering disciplines, including: Aerospace, aeronautical, and astronautical engineering. Agricultural engineering. Architectural engineering. Biochemical engineering. Biomedical and bioengineering. Biological and biosystems engineering. Chemical engineering. Civil engineering. Computer engineering. Construction engineering. Electrical and communications engineering. Electromechanical engineering. Engineering mechanics. Engineering physics and applied physics. Environmental and environmental health engineering. Geological and geophysical engineering. Industrial engineering. Manufacturing engineering. Materials engineering. Mechanical engineering. Mechatronics, robotics, and automation engineering. Metallurgical engineering. Mining and mineral engineering. Naval architecture and marine engineering. Nuclear engineering. Ocean engineering. Operations research. Petroleum engineering. Polymer and plastics engineering. Surveying engineering. Systems engineering. Textile sciences and engineering. Engineering Technologies Relevant technology-related areas include: Drafting and design technology. Electrical, electronic, and communications engineering technology. General engineering technologies. Industrial production technologies. Instrumentation technology. Mining and petroleum technologies. Nanotechnology. Quality control and safety technologies. Physical Sciences Students studying physical sciences may also be eligible, with listed areas including: Astronomy and astrophysics. Atmospheric sciences and meteorology. Chemistry. Geological and earth sciences. Hydrology and water resources science. Materials science. Physics. The extensive list demonstrates that the position is multidisciplinary and is not restricted exclusively to aerospace engineering students. Who Can Apply? According to the opportunity listing, eligible applicants must be students and must meet NASA s stated citizenship and academic-level requirements. The listed academic levels include: Undergraduate freshmen. Undergraduate sophomores. Undergraduate juniors. Undergraduate seniors. Graduate students pursuing a master s degree. The NASA internship description also states that its educational hands-on internships are available to undergraduate and graduate students aged 16 and above . The opportunity specifically lists U.S. citizenship as a requirement . Therefore, applicants should carefully confirm their citizenship and academic eligibility before beginning the application process. Countries and Geographic Eligibility This particular opportunity is not open globally . The listing specifically states: Citizenship: U.S. Citizen Only Applicants therefore need to be U.S. citizens to qualify for this specific Texas Aerospace Scholars position. The work location is Houston, Texas, at NASA Johnson Space Center, and the position is in-person. International applicants who are not U.S. citizens should therefore not assume that they can apply simply because they meet the academic or professional requirements. NASA maintains separate eligibility requirements for different internship programs, so prospective applicants should always review the eligibility information attached to the specific opportunity they are applying for. Race and Ethnicity Eligibility The opportunity listing provided does not specify a race, ethnicity, or racial group as an eligibility requirement. Accordingly, no race-specific eligibility restriction is stated in the opportunity description . The clearly stated nationality requirement is U.S. citizenship, together with the academic and student requirements described in the listing. Applicants should rely on the official NASA application information for the authoritative eligibility requirements. Why the Research Brief Component Matters The research briefs are not simply administrative documents. According to the opportunity description, they are intended to give Texas Aerospace Scholars students structured, NASA-focused research opportunities. The materials will help students: Explore NASA-related scientific and technical topics. Understand aspects of human space exploration. Connect classroom learning with real-world aerospace objectives. Investigate Moon-to-Mars exploration concepts. Develop research and analytical skills. Explore potential aerospace and STEM career pathways. This means the intern s work can have an educational impact beyond the immediate internship. By producing accessible and well-researched materials, the selected student will contribute to how younger learners encounter NASA s exploration objectives. A Strong Opportunity for Communication and STEM Students One of the distinctive features of this position is its combination of communications and STEM. A communication or journalism student does not necessarily need to be an aerospace engineer to see the relevance of the opportunity. The position specifically requires someone who can research technical information and communicate it effectively to a younger audience. Likewise, an engineering, physics, astronomy, chemistry, or other STEM student with strong writing and communication abilities may find the role particularly valuable. The position therefore sits at the intersection of the following: Science communication. STEM education. Aerospace exploration. Technical writing. Research. Educational content development. Digital communication. Graphic design. Student engagement. NASA mission education. How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application Prospective applicants should carefully demonstrate how their academic background, technical abilities, communication experience, and interest in NASA or STEM education align with the responsibilities of the position. Useful areas to emphasize include: Demonstrate Research Ability Applicants should highlight academic research projects, research papers, independent projects, laboratory work, or other experiences that demonstrate their ability to find, evaluate, organize, and communicate information. Highlight Writing Experience Writing experience can come from academic papers, journalism, newsletters, blogs, reports, educational materials, research publications, communications work, or other relevant projects. Show Experience Explaining Complex Ideas Applicants should provide examples of situations where they translated technical, scientific, academic, or specialized information into language that a broader audience could understand. Demonstrate Editing Skills Proofreading, editing, content review, quality assurance, and publication experience can all demonstrate suitability for a role that involves developing professional research briefs and educational materials. Mention Digital and Design Skills Applicants with experience in graphic design, digital content creation, visual communication, presentation design, or educational media should make those capabilities clear. Highlight Teamwork Examples of successful collaboration with lecturers, researchers, colleagues, student groups, mentors, technical experts, or project teams can strengthen an application. Demonstrate Organization Because the position involves multiple deliverables and projects, applicants should demonstrate their ability to organize deadlines, prioritize assignments, and manage competing responsibilities. Connect Your Background to STEM or Aerospace Applicants with experience in STEM education, aerospace, NASA-related activities, science communication, engineering projects, robotics, space science, or related areas should clearly demonstrate this connection. Application Timeline The registration period for this opportunity is: Registration Opens: June 12, 2026 Application Deadline: September 14, 2026 Program Session: Spring 2027 Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing application materials in advance can allow sufficient time to review eligibility requirements, academic information, supporting materials, and other application details. title: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027: Apply for Graduate Study at the University of Hawai‘i
summary: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from eligible students seeking to pursue graduate-level study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa in the United States. The fellowship is offered by the East-West Center (EWC) and is designed to support graduate study in academic fields that are relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center. The fellowship is awarded through an international competition , giving eligible applicants from the United States and selected countries across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia an opportunity to compete for graduate study support. For prospective applicants, this is an important opportunity to combine advanced academic study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader educational, cultural and international community associated with the East-West Center. The application deadline is December 1, 2026 . East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 at a Glance Opportunity: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Academic year: 2026–2027 Host institution: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa Host country: United States Study level: Graduate Selection method: International competition Opening period: August 2026 Application deadline: December 1, 2026 University admission deadline for new UH Mānoa applicants: December 1, 2026 Supporting documents deadline: January 10, following the application deadline Eligible applicants: Citizens or permanent residents of the specified eligible countries and territories Academic requirement: Four-year bachelor’s degree or equivalent General GPA requirement: Minimum 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or equivalent Study location: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa Application contact: scholarships@eastwestcenter.org What Is the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship is a graduate education opportunity supporting students undertaking advanced study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa . The fellowship focuses on graduate study in fields that are relevant to the objectives and mission of the East-West Center. Successful applicants therefore have the opportunity not only to pursue graduate education but also to become part of an international academic environment bringing together students and professionals connected to the United States and the Asia-Pacific region. The fellowship is awarded annually through an international competitive process. Applicants should therefore expect their academic background, qualifications and overall suitability for the fellowship to be considered alongside applications from other eligible candidates. For the 2026–2027 academic year, applications are being invited during the 2026 application cycle. Why Consider the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? Graduate education in the United States can provide students with access to advanced academic training, international exposure, research opportunities and professional networks. The East-West Center fellowship is particularly significant because it connects graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader East-West Center environment. Successful fellows can therefore benefit from an academic experience situated within an institution whose work focuses on relationships and understanding among the United States and countries and peoples of the Asia-Pacific region. The opportunity may be particularly relevant to students whose academic and professional interests intersect with areas connected to the East-West Center s goals and objectives. Where Will Fellows Study? The fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa , commonly known as UH Mānoa. The University of Hawai‘i s graduate application process is separate from the East-West Center fellowship application. This means prospective applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa need to complete the relevant University of Hawai‘i admission process in addition to the East-West Center fellowship application. Applicants should therefore treat the two processes as connected but distinct requirements. Who Can Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? Eligibility is geographically restricted. The East-West Center states that individuals who are citizens or permanent residents of the specified countries and territories may apply. The eligible locations are divided into the following groups: 1. United States Citizens and permanent residents of the United States are eligible to apply. 2. Pacific Region Eligible Pacific locations include the following: American Samoa Australia Cook Islands Federated States of Micronesia Fiji French Polynesia Guam Kiribati Marshall Islands Nauru New Caledonia New Zealand Niue Northern Marianas Palau Papua New Guinea Samoa Solomon Islands Tokelau Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu Wallis Futuna Islands 3. Southeast Asia Eligible Southeast Asian countries include the following: Brunei Cambodia Indonesia Laos Malaysia Myanmar Philippines Singapore Thailand Timor-Leste Vietnam 4. South Asia Eligible South Asian countries include: Afghanistan Bangladesh Bhutan India Iran Maldives Nepal Pakistan Sri Lanka 5. East Asia Eligible East Asian countries and territories include: China Hong Kong Japan Macau Mongolia North Korea South Korea Russia Taiwan Important Eligibility Note for African Applicants Applicants should carefully review the geographic eligibility requirement before investing time in the application. The eligible-country list provided by the East-West Center does not include African countries . This means applicants from countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Ethiopia and other African countries are not included in the eligible-country list provided for this fellowship. There is also no separate race or ethnicity-based eligibility category stated in the information provided. Eligibility is primarily determined by citizenship or permanent residency, academic qualifications and other fellowship requirements . Academic Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy specific academic requirements before the fellowship begins. For graduate programs, applicants must have obtained a four-year bachelor s degree or equivalent . The degree must be from either: An accredited college or university in the United States; or A recognized institution of higher learning outside the United States. This means applicants with undergraduate qualifications obtained outside the United States can still be considered, provided their qualification is recognized as equivalent to the required four-year bachelor s degree. Minimum GPA Requirement Applicants are generally expected to have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale , or an equivalent academic performance. The GPA requirement applies to: The applicant s last four semesters of undergraduate study; or The applicant s last six quarters of undergraduate study; and All post-baccalaureate academic work , where applicable. This is an important distinction because applicants should not assume that only their cumulative undergraduate GPA will be considered. Applicants who have completed postgraduate coursework should also take their post-baccalaureate academic performance into account when assessing their competitiveness. What If Your University Uses a Different Grading System? The East-West Center recognizes that universities outside the United States may use different grading systems. The stated requirement is a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent . Therefore, applicants whose universities do not use the U.S. 4.0 GPA system should consider how their academic results correspond to the required standard and provide accurate academic documentation during the application process. Applicants should avoid independently converting grades in a way that misrepresents their academic record. Where official documentation or institutional guidance is available, applicants should follow the appropriate process. Fields of Study The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i in fields relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center . This means prospective applicants should not focus only on whether a graduate program is available at UH Mānoa. They should also consider whether their intended field of study aligns with the broader purpose and objectives of the East-West Center. Applicants are encouraged to review the fellowship s official information, frequently asked questions and award details before submitting an application. How the Application Process Works The fellowship application process involves more than simply completing the East-West Center application. Applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester. Consequently, prospective applicants should plan their application in two parallel tracks: Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship. Apply for admission to the appropriate University of Hawai‘i graduate program. Both processes should be planned carefully because missing a university admission requirement can affect the overall application timeline. University of Hawai‘i Admission Requirement If you are not already enrolled as a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, you must apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester by December 1, 2026 . The University of Hawai‘i launches its online graduate application system on August 1 each year for admission the following year. Prospective applicants should therefore begin preparing their university application well before the fellowship deadline. This is particularly important for applicants applying to graduate departments that may have additional admission requirements. Supporting Documents Deadline The East-West Center also provides an important date after the main application deadline. To ensure timely processing of the East-West Center application, supporting documents for both the University of Hawai‘i admissions office and the relevant department applications must be completed by January 10 . This requirement applies regardless of whether the particular UH departmental deadline falls after January 10. Applicants should therefore not assume that a later departmental deadline automatically gives them additional time for the East-West Center process. A good strategy is to aim to complete all required university and departmental materials before January 10. Application Forms Required The East-West Center provides specific application forms that prospective applicants should review and complete as applicable. title: GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program: Grants of Up to $300,000 for Civil Society Organizations Leading Environmental Solutions
summary: Civil society organizations (CSOs) working on climate change, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture, ecosystem restoration, low-carbon development, pollution reduction, waste management, food security, and sustainable urban development have an opportunity to access significant funding through the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program . The program builds on the experience of the Global Environment Facility Small Grants Program (GEF SGP) and is designed to identify, recognize, and support innovative environmental solutions developed and implemented by civil society organizations and local actors. Unlike traditional small-grant approaches, the CSO Challenge Program is intended for organizations that have already demonstrated technical and organizational capacity and have a proven record of achievement and impact. Successful applicants can receive grants of up to US$300,000 to support projects lasting up to 24 months . The funding is particularly relevant to organizations seeking to take an existing environmental solution to the next level through replication, adaptation, scaling, and expanded impact . Opportunity Overview The GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program is an initiative focused on strengthening high-impact environmental action led by civil society organizations. The program recognizes that communities and CSOs are often closest to the environmental challenges affecting their regions. These organizations frequently understand local ecosystems, livelihoods, cultural contexts, and community needs better than outside institutions. However, organizations with successful ideas may lack the financial resources needed to replicate or scale those solutions. The CSO Challenge Program is intended to address this gap by providing larger grants and tailored support to organizations with demonstrated experience and promising approaches. The program s central objective is to: Identify, reward, and support high-impact innovative environmental approaches and solutions spearheaded by civil society organizations and actors. What Is the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program? The Global Environment Facility Small Grants Program (GEF SGP) has supported community-based environmental and conservation initiatives for decades. The CSO Challenge Program builds upon that experience while introducing a funding approach aimed at organizations that are ready to move beyond individual community-level projects. Rather than primarily supporting organizations at the earliest stages of development, the program targets CSOs that already have: Relevant technical expertise. Strong organizational capacity. Experience implementing environmental initiatives. Evidence of successful results. A demonstrated record of impact. An environmental solution or approach with potential for wider application. The ability to manage a larger grant. A clear pathway toward replication, adaptation, or scaling. Through grants of up to US$300,000 , the program provides an opportunity for established CSOs to expand solutions that have already demonstrated promise. Funding Amount and Project Duration Eligible organizations can apply for grants of up to: US$300,000 Projects supported under the program can run for up to: 24 months This funding level is significantly larger than traditional small grants and is intended to help organizations transition successful approaches from individual projects into broader initiatives capable of generating greater environmental and community impact. Applicants should therefore demonstrate not simply that their project is important, but also why additional investment is necessary and how the proposed funding will contribute to measurable growth, replication, adaptation, or scaling. What Types of Projects Does the Program Fund? The CSO Challenge Program supports initiatives that can demonstrate potential for wider environmental impact. In particular, funding can support organizations seeking to: 1. Replicate Proven Models Organizations can seek funding to reproduce an environmental solution that has already demonstrated success in one community, ecosystem, location, or context. Replication may involve taking an existing model and introducing it to: New communities. New geographic areas. New ecosystems. Similar environmental contexts. Different local or national settings. The applicant should be able to demonstrate why the existing model is successful and why it has potential to work in the proposed new setting. 2. Adapt Existing Solutions Environmental solutions do not always work identically in every location. The program therefore supports efforts to adapt proven approaches to local circumstances, including differences in: Ecosystems. Climate conditions. Community needs. Local economies. Governance structures. Cultural practices. Natural-resource availability. Livelihood systems. An organization may therefore propose to modify an existing successful approach so that it becomes effective in a different local context. 3. Test Scaling Approaches The program also supports organizations seeking to determine how a promising environmental innovation can be expanded. Scaling can involve increasing the number of communities reached, expanding geographic coverage, reaching additional beneficiaries, strengthening implementation systems, or developing partnerships that allow an established solution to reach a substantially larger population. The emphasis is on moving beyond isolated success toward approaches that can generate broader and more sustainable environmental outcomes. Five Strategic Priority Areas The program welcomes applications from CSOs working in five strategic areas. 1. Community-Based Management of Threatened Ecosystems and Species This priority area focuses on empowering communities to protect, restore, and sustainably manage ecosystems and species facing environmental pressure. Potential initiatives may involve: Biodiversity conservation. Habitat restoration. Community-based conservation. Protection of threatened species. Ecosystem restoration. Sustainable natural-resource management. Community stewardship of important ecosystems. Conservation initiatives involving local communities. The program recognizes that communities can play an important role in protecting biodiversity when they have the knowledge, resources, partnerships, and incentives required to manage natural resources sustainably. 2. Sustainable Agriculture and Fisheries and Food Security The program also supports approaches that connect environmental sustainability with food production and community livelihoods. Relevant initiatives may address: Sustainable agriculture. Sustainable fisheries. Food security. Natural-resource conservation. Climate-resilient food systems. Sustainable production practices. Community-based fisheries management. Agricultural approaches that protect ecosystems. Projects should demonstrate how environmental protection can be integrated with sustainable livelihoods and food production. 3. Low-Carbon Energy Access Another priority area is expanding access to low-carbon energy while generating wider social and environmental benefits. Relevant projects may focus on innovative approaches that: Expand access to clean energy. Reduce dependence on high-carbon energy sources. Improve energy access for underserved communities. Support sustainable local development. Generate social and economic benefits alongside environmental gains. Organizations working on community-based low-carbon energy solutions may therefore find this funding area particularly relevant. 4. Chemicals and Waste Management The program supports initiatives designed to reduce pollution and strengthen environmentally responsible approaches to chemicals and waste management. Potential areas of intervention include: Waste reduction. Waste management. Pollution prevention. Community-based waste solutions. Safer management of chemicals. Circular approaches to resource use. Initiatives protecting human and environmental health. Projects should demonstrate how the proposed approach can contribute to reduced pollution and improved environmental outcomes. 5. Sustainable Urban Solutions The fifth strategic priority focuses on innovation that can make cities and urban communities more sustainable and resilient. Potential initiatives may address: Sustainable urban development. Urban environmental challenges. Climate resilience. Sustainable resource management. Urban waste. Low-carbon urban solutions. Community-based approaches to urban sustainability. Environmental innovation in cities. This area is particularly relevant to CSOs developing solutions to environmental problems associated with rapidly growing urban populations. Who Can Apply? The program is specifically designed for civil society organizations , rather than individual applicants. Applicant organizations must satisfy the eligibility requirements established by the program. Civil Society Organization Requirement An applicant must be a legally established civil society organization . The organization must have: Legal status; and A bank account held in the organization s name. This means individuals applying independently are not the primary target of this funding opportunity. Organizations should ensure that their legal registration and financial arrangements meet the program s requirements before submitting an application. Location Requirement Applicants must be based in a GEF SGP eligible recipient country . Furthermore, the initiatives being proposed for replication or scaling must also be based in eligible GEF recipient countries. The program therefore has a defined geographic eligibility framework rather than being open to organizations from every country worldwide. Eligible Countries and Regions GEF recipient countries covered by the program are organized into four broad regions: Africa — 54 countries Latin America and the Caribbean — 33 countries Eastern Europe, Caucasus and Central Asia (EECCA) — 18 countries Asia-Pacific and Oceania — 39 countries Applicants should consult the official full country list before beginning an application because eligibility is determined according to the program s designated GEF recipient-country framework. What Makes This Opportunity Different? One of the most important features of the CSO Challenge Program is its focus on organizations with demonstrated achievement and impact . The program is not simply seeking ideas that sound innovative on paper. It is designed to support organizations that can demonstrate that their approaches have already produced meaningful results and have potential for greater impact. This makes evidence especially important. A strong applicant should be able to demonstrate: What environmental problem it is addressing. What solution it has developed or implemented. Where the solution has already been implemented. What results have been achieved. Why the solution is innovative or particularly effective. What evidence demonstrates its success. Why the solution can be replicated, adapted, or scaled. What additional funding is required to achieve expansion. How the proposed project will generate measurable environmental benefits. How communities and relevant stakeholders will participate. Inclusion Is a Major Program Priority The CSO Challenge Program strongly encourages projects that meaningfully engage: Women. Youth. Indigenous Peoples. Local communities. This means applicants should consider inclusion not merely as an additional component of a project, but as part of the design and implementation of the proposed environmental solution. Organizations should demonstrate how relevant groups will participate in decision-making, implementation, knowledge generation, resource management, or other aspects of the initiative. Projects that integrate environmental impact with meaningful community participation may therefore align particularly well with the program s objectives. Program Goals The CSO Challenge Program has four major goals. Recognize Innovative Environmental Initiatives The program seeks to identify and recognize environmental approaches that demonstrate strong potential for impact. It particularly values initiatives that can be replicated or scaled beyond their original location. Strengthen Organizational Capacity and Impact Selected CSOs can receive support aimed at strengthening their ability to design, implement, and scale innovative environmental solutions. This reflects the program s broader understanding that scaling an environmental solution requires more than money alone. Organizations may also need stronger systems, technical expertise, partnerships, knowledge, and implementation capacity. Promote Peer-to-Peer Learning and Partnerships The program seeks to facilitate knowledge exchange and collaboration among: Civil society organizations. Governments. Donors. Private-sector actors. Other relevant stakeholders. Peer learning can allow organizations to learn from environmental solutions implemented in other communities and countries while also sharing their own experiences. Support Inclusive Environmental Action The program promotes environmental approaches that meaningfully include women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and local communities. This reflects the principle that environmental solutions are more likely to generate sustainable outcomes when the people directly affected by environmental challenges are involved in developing and implementing responses. Organizations Behind the Program The initiative is supported by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and led by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) , in partnership with RTI International . Global Environment Facility The GEF brings together several multilateral funds working to address major global environmental challenges through integrated approaches. According to the information provided by the program, the GEF has supplied more than US$26 billion in financing and mobilized an additional US$148 billion for country-driven priority projects over more than three decades. International Union for Conservation of Nature IUCN is a major international environmental organization with government and NGO members and a global network of volunteer experts. Its work focuses on finding practical solutions to environmental and development challenges, including biodiversity conservation, ecosystem protection, and sustainable development. RTI International RTI International is an independent scientific research institute that works across multiple disciplines, including social sciences, statistics, data, laboratory sciences, engineering, and other technical fields. Its partnership with the initiative brings additional research and technical expertise to the program. Why CSOs Should Consider Applying For an established environmental organization, a grant of up to US$300,000 can provide substantial resources for expanding a proven solution. The opportunity can be particularly valuable for organizations that have already completed pilot projects and now need funding to move toward larger-scale implementation. Potential benefits include: Significant financial support for environmental initiatives. Resources for replication and scaling. Opportunities to expand successful approaches into new locations. Support for adapting solutions to new contexts. Opportunities for organizational strengthening. Increased visibility for innovative environmental work. Opportunities for peer-to-peer learning. Potential partnerships with governments, donors, and private-sector actors. Greater environmental and community impact. How Applicants Can Prepare Organizations interested in the program should begin by assessing their readiness. Step 1: Confirm Organizational Eligibility First, verify that the organization: Is a legally recognized CSO. Has a bank account in the organization s name. Is based in an eligible GEF recipient country. Meets the program s organizational requirements. Step 2: Identify the Environmental Solution Applicants should clearly define the environmental solution they want to replicate, adapt, or scale. Avoid presenting only a broad environmental problem. Instead, explain the specific approach the organization has developed and the evidence showing that it works. Step 3: Document Previous Results Evidence of previous impact is particularly important for this program. Organizations should collect relevant information such as: Previous project outcomes. Environmental indicators. Community-level results. Number of people or communities reached. Conservation achievements. Restoration results. Changes in resource use. Partnerships established. Lessons learned. Monitoring and evaluation findings. Step 4: Develop a Clear Scaling Strategy Applicants should explain what will happen if additional funding is received. For example, will the project: Reach additional communities? Expand into another region? Replicate an existing model? Adapt an approach for a new ecosystem? Increase the number of beneficiaries? Establish new partnerships? Develop a more sustainable implementation model? The scaling pathway should be realistic and supported by evidence. Step 5: Integrate Inclusion Applicants should explain how the project will meaningfully engage women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and local communities where relevant. This could include participation in: Project design. Governance. Implementation. Monitoring. Decision-making. Knowledge sharing. Livelihood activities. Conservation activities. Step 6: Review the Official Guidelines Before preparing a final submission, organizations should carefully consult the official Guidelines for Applicants and the complete list of GEF recipient countries. The guidelines should be treated as the authoritative source for detailed application requirements. Important Considerations for Applicants Organizations should avoid assuming that environmental relevance alone guarantees eligibility. A proposal should demonstrate a strong connection between: Existing success → proven solution → proposed expansion → measurable impact Applicants should also ensure that the requested funding is appropriate for the proposed activities and project duration. Because the program prioritizes replication, adaptation, and scaling, organizations with only an undeveloped concept and no demonstrated record of implementation may not be as well aligned as organizations with proven environmental solutions. APPLY HERE Deadline Deadline: 15th September 2026 Applicants should check the official GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program website and the current application guidelines for the latest application timeline, submission window, and any applicable deadlines before preparing or submitting an application. Official Application and Further Information Applicants should consult the official program resources for the complete eligibility requirements, country list, application guidance, and submission information. Applicants should also review the official Guidelines for Applicants and the GEF Recipient Countries list before proceeding. Visit HERE to learn more about the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program. Conclusion The GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program represents a significant funding opportunity for established civil society organizations that have already demonstrated that their environmental approaches can work and are now ready to achieve broader impact. With grants of up to US$300,000 and support for projects lasting up to 24 months , the program is designed to help organizations move beyond isolated projects and expand successful environmental solutions through replication, adaptation, and scaling. Its emphasis on biodiversity, sustainable food systems, low-carbon energy, pollution and waste management, and sustainable urban development makes the opportunity relevant to a broad range of environmental CSOs across eligible GEF recipient countries. Organizations considering this opportunity should focus on demonstrating evidence of previous impact, organizational capacity, a credible scaling strategy, environmental significance, and meaningful community inclusion . Most importantly, prospective applicants should verify their country s eligibility and carefully review the official applicant guidelines before developing their proposal. For organizations with a proven environmental solution and a clear strategy for expanding its impact, the CSO Challenge Program could provide the financial and partnership support needed to transform a successful local initiative into a much larger environmental solution. title: Fully Funded PhD in Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy at Utrecht University: €4,051 Monthly Salary
summary: Utrecht University in the Netherlands is inviting applications for a fully funded four-year PhD position in Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy . The opportunity is hosted by the Faculty of Geosciences , within the Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning , and is designed for highly motivated researchers interested in innovation, international mobility, human capital, economic geography, and the future of Europe’s knowledge and innovation systems. This is a particularly attractive opportunity for prospective doctoral researchers who want to pursue an interdisciplinary research career while working with large-scale datasets and internationally recognised researchers. The successful candidate will investigate how Europe’s ambitions for technological innovation, competitiveness, resilience, and strategic autonomy are connected to the movement of highly skilled international talent, particularly people who have completed PhDs in STEM-related fields. Unlike a conventional scholarship that simply provides a study allowance, this opportunity is a paid PhD employment position . The selected candidate will be employed by Utrecht University and receive a gross monthly salary, alongside holiday pay, a year-end bonus, pension arrangements, leave benefits, and professional development opportunities. Host Institution Utrecht University Faculty Faculty of Geosciences Department Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning Research Sections The successful candidate will be based in the Economic Geography Section of the Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning, while working closely with the Innovation Studies Section at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development . The two research groups provide an interdisciplinary environment combining economic geography, innovation studies, migration research, and related social science disciplines. PhD Research Topic Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy The PhD project focuses on an increasingly important question: How does Europe’s ability to innovate and maintain strategic autonomy depend on the international mobility of highly skilled talent? Talent has become a critical resource for modern innovation systems. Highly educated researchers and professionals contribute to scientific discovery, technological development, entrepreneurship, and knowledge transfer. At the same time, Europe and other regions are facing major changes in the international movement of skilled workers and researchers. Geopolitical tensions, migration restrictions, national security concerns, and changing international relationships may influence where highly skilled people choose to study, work, conduct research, and build their careers. These developments could have significant consequences for global knowledge networks and innovation. The PhD project therefore seeks to understand the relationship between: Global talent mobility International migration Doctoral education Human capital Innovation Scientific research Technological development Economic geography Institutional environments Europe’s strategic autonomy International knowledge networks A particular focus will be placed on STEM PhD recipients , who are important contributors to science- and technology-based innovation. What Will the PhD Research Investigate? The project will examine how doctoral training, international mobility, and institutional environments influence where knowledge is produced and where that knowledge is eventually transformed into technological and economic value. The research will connect perspectives from economic geography and innovation studies to investigate questions surrounding the movement of global talent and the consequences of that movement for innovation systems. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop unique datasets and use quantitative and mixed-method research approaches. The research may involve combining several types of information, including: PhD recipient data Career information Publication records Patent data Survey data Administrative data Online data Individual mobility information Other relevant sources concerning career trajectories and preferences This makes the position particularly suitable for applicants who are interested in data-intensive academic research and interdisciplinary approaches. Main Responsibilities of the PhD Candidate The successful applicant will be expected to take an active role in designing and implementing the research project. Key responsibilities include: 1. Designing the Research Project You will develop research questions and research strategies around global talent interdependencies, international mobility, innovation, and Europe’s strategic autonomy . The project provides room for the PhD researcher to develop their own academic expertise while contributing to the broader research objectives. 2. Collecting and Analysing Large-Scale Data A major part of the position involves working with large datasets. Potential sources include: Publication data Patent information Career data Administrative datasets Survey information Online data Other sources relevant to international mobility and innovation Applicants with experience handling large-scale datasets and quantitative research will therefore be particularly well positioned. 3. Writing Research Papers The successful candidate will produce academic research papers that contribute to the completion of the PhD. The research is expected to meet the academic standards required for doctoral research and contribute to scholarly discussions surrounding migration, innovation, geography, and human capital. 4. Presenting Research The PhD candidate will have opportunities to present their research at: International conferences National conferences Academic workshops Research seminars Other scholarly events This will help the candidate develop their academic profile and professional research network. 5. Completing a Doctoral Dissertation The ultimate objective is to complete a PhD dissertation within the four-year period. The position is specifically structured with the intention that the successful candidate obtains a doctorate during the appointment. 6. Contributing to Teaching The candidate will also contribute to teaching activities within the department. Applicants should therefore be interested not only in research but also in developing their teaching and academic communication skills. Who Is This PhD Position For? The position is aimed at prospective doctoral researchers with a strong interest in: Innovation Human capital International migration Global talent mobility Economic geography Innovation studies Development studies Sociology Economics Geography Science and technology studies Related social science disciplines Utrecht University welcomes applicants from diverse disciplinary backgrounds , provided they can demonstrate a strong fit with the research project. Academic Qualifications and Skills Required Applicants should demonstrate a strong motivation for academic research and a genuine interest in the relationship between global talent and innovation systems. Strong Research Motivation Candidates should be curious about the factors influencing global talent mobility and the consequences of international mobility for innovation and knowledge production. Quantitative Research Skills Applicants should have quantitative analytical skills, including experience with: Data analysis Statistics Quantitative research methods Large-scale datasets Experience with web scraping is an advantage. Experience With Multiple Data Sources The project involves combining different types of data. Applicants who have experience working with several sources of information will therefore have an advantage. Relevant experience may include working with: Administrative data Patent databases Publication databases Surveys Online data Career datasets Interdisciplinary Interest Applicants should be interested in connecting different academic perspectives, particularly geography and innovation studies . An interdisciplinary mindset will be important because the project sits at the intersection of several research fields. Strong Academic Writing Candidates must demonstrate strong academic writing skills. A writing sample such as a Master’s thesis or comparable academic document is required as part of the application. Independent Working Ability The successful candidate should be capable of working independently while also contributing effectively to a collaborative and international research environment. English Language Proficiency Applicants must have excellent spoken and written English at approximately C1 level . Teaching Interest Candidates should also demonstrate motivation to develop their teaching skills. Funding and Salary One of the strongest features of this opportunity is that it is a paid PhD position . The selected candidate will receive a gross monthly salary ranging from: €3,204 to €4,051 per month for full-time employment, depending on the applicable salary progression under salary scale P of the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU) . The position involves a working week of: 36–40 hours per week. This means that successful applicants are employed as PhD researchers rather than simply receiving a conventional scholarship stipend. Employment Benefits In addition to the monthly salary, Utrecht University offers a range of employment benefits. These include: 8% holiday pay 8.3% year-end bonus Pension scheme Partially paid parental leave Flexible employment conditions Professional development opportunities Various types of leave Sports and cultural activity arrangements Options to tailor employment conditions through the Terms of Employment Options Model The university also provides opportunities for employees to continue developing their academic and professional skills. Duration of the PhD Position The position initially covers one year . Following a successful assessment during the first year, the appointment can be extended to a total of four years . The position is specifically intended to result in the completion of a doctoral degree within this period. Applicants should therefore understand that the full four-year continuation is dependent on successful assessment after the first year. Research Environment at Utrecht University The successful candidate will join an internationally oriented academic environment. The PhD researcher will be based in the Economic Geography Section and work closely with the Innovation Studies Section . The research groups are described as internationally leading in their respective disciplines, creating an environment where researchers can develop their expertise and work at the frontier of academic research. The collaboration between economic geography and innovation studies provides an opportunity to investigate complex questions from multiple perspectives. About Utrecht University Utrecht University is one of the Netherlands major research universities. The university s broad ambition is centred around creating a better future through leading research and inspiring teaching. Researchers across different disciplines collaborate around major strategic themes, including: Dynamics of Youth Institutions for Open Societies Life Sciences Pathways to Sustainability The university promotes interdisciplinary collaboration and international research. About the Faculty of Geosciences The Faculty of Geosciences studies the Earth from its core to its surface, including the ways humans use space and natural resources. The faculty places strong emphasis on sustainability and innovation . It has approximately: 3,400 BSc and MSc students 720 staff members The Faculty of Geosciences consists of four departments: Earth Sciences Human Geography and Spatial Planning Physical Geography Sustainable Development This PhD position is located within the Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning . Supervisors The successful candidate will work under the supervision of: Dr Burcu Özgün Dr Giovanna Capponi Professor Carolina Castaldi Their supervision will support the candidate in developing the research project and progressing toward completion of the doctoral dissertation. Application Deadline The deadline for applications is: 14 September 2026 Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the stated deadline. Because this is a competitive PhD position, candidates are encouraged not to wait until the final day to prepare and submit their documents. What You Need to Submit Applicants must submit their application through the official Utrecht University application system. The application should include the following: 1. Motivation Letter A letter explaining your motivation and qualifications in relation to the PhD position. Your letter should demonstrate why you are interested in: Global talent mobility Innovation Human capital International mobility Economic geography Europe’s strategic autonomy It should also explain why your academic background and skills make you a suitable candidate. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide an up-to-date CV outlining their: Academic background Research experience Quantitative skills Publications, where applicable Relevant projects Professional experience Technical or analytical skills 3. Writing Sample Applicants must provide a writing sample demonstrating their academic ability. The university preferably requests a Master’s thesis or comparable academic document . Applicants should select a piece of work that demonstrates strong analytical reasoning, research ability, academic writing, and methodological competence. 4. Two Referees Applicants must provide the names and contact details of two referees . Recommendation letters are not required at the initial application stage. They will be requested only from candidates who are shortlisted for an interview. Interview Timeline The first round of interviews is scheduled to take place during: The last week of September 2026 Applicants should therefore be available during this period if shortlisted. Requirements for International Applicants International applicants are welcome to apply. Candidates who hold an international, non-Dutch Master s degree may be asked to provide their: Bachelor s degree certificate Master s degree certificate Corresponding grade lists These documents should be provided in English if the applicant is selected for the position. Visa and Work Permit Information International candidates who require a visa or work permit to work in the Netherlands should take the immigration timeline seriously. Utrecht University notes that applicants requiring a visa or work permit need at least four months of processing time after selection and acceptance . The university will assist successful international candidates through its International Service Desk (ISD) . This is an important consideration for candidates applying from outside the Netherlands. Housing in Utrecht International applicants should also be aware that finding accommodation in or near Utrecht is the applicant s own responsibility. The International Service Desk may provide advice and assistance regarding housing, but applicants should not assume that accommodation will automatically be provided. Utrecht University warns that the housing market is currently tight. Candidates are therefore encouraged to begin considering accommodation arrangements as early as possible if they are eventually selected. Who Can Apply? This opportunity is open to qualified applicants from diverse nationalities and international backgrounds . The vacancy does not specify that applicants must come from a particular country, race, or continent. International applicants, including candidates from outside the Netherlands, can therefore be considered provided they meet the academic, research, language, and other requirements of the position. The university explicitly states its commitment to an inclusive working environment and welcomes colleagues with different backgrounds, perspectives, and identities. Important Knowledge Security Screening Applicants should also be aware that knowledge security screening may form part of the selection procedure for academic staff . According to Utrecht University, this is intended, among other purposes, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. Candidates whose research or background falls within areas requiring such screening may therefore be subject to additional procedures. Why This PhD Opportunity Is Worth Considering This position offers several advantages for researchers seeking an international academic career. 1. Paid Doctoral Employment Instead of relying on a traditional scholarship stipend, the successful candidate is employed by Utrecht University and receives a monthly salary. 2. Four-Year Doctoral Pathway The position is designed to support completion of a doctorate within four years, subject to successful assessment after the first year. 3. International Research Environment The candidate will work in an internationally oriented academic environment with researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds. 4. Interdisciplinary Research The project combines economic geography and innovation studies, making it particularly relevant for researchers interested in interdisciplinary research. 5. Data-Intensive Research Experience The PhD offers the opportunity to work with large-scale datasets and combine sources such as publications, patents, career records, surveys, administrative data, and online information. 6. Conference and Research Exposure The candidate will have opportunities to present research at conferences, workshops, and seminars, helping build an international academic network. 7. Teaching Development The successful candidate will contribute to departmental teaching and develop academic teaching skills. 8. Professional Development Utrecht University provides various professional development opportunities and employment benefits to help staff continue developing their careers. How to Make Your Application Stronger Although meeting the minimum requirements is essential, applicants should also focus on demonstrating a clear fit with the specific research project. Connect Your Background to the Project Do not simply describe your academic history. Explain how your previous education, dissertation, research experience, employment, or projects have prepared you to investigate global talent, innovation, mobility, or related topics. Demonstrate Your Quantitative Skills If you have experience with: Statistical analysis Econometrics Data visualisation Programming Web scraping Large datasets Research databases make this clear in your CV and motivation letter. Highlight Relevant Research If your Master s thesis or previous research relates to migration, innovation, human capital, international mobility, economic geography, development, science, technology, or related fields, explain the connection. Choose Your Writing Sample Carefully Your writing sample is an important part of the application. Select a document that demonstrates: Strong research design Clear argumentation Analytical thinking Academic writing Appropriate methodology Ability to interpret evidence Explain Your Interdisciplinary Interest The project crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries. Applicants should therefore demonstrate an ability and willingness to engage with perspectives from both geography and innovation studies. Applicants should ensure that all documents clearly demonstrate their suitability for the research project.
