Apply HERE Conclusion The Utrecht University PhD in Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy is a strong opportunity for researchers who want to build an academic career at the intersection of international migration, innovation, human capital, economic geography, and global talent mobility . The position combines doctoral research with paid university employment, offering a gross monthly salary of €3,204 to €4,051 , holiday pay, a year-end bonus, pension benefits, professional development opportunities, and the possibility of completing a doctorate within four years. The research itself is highly relevant to contemporary debates about Europe s competitiveness, technological innovation, international migration, knowledge networks, and strategic autonomy. Candidates will have the opportunity to work with large-scale datasets, publish research, attend academic conferences, contribute to teaching, and collaborate with researchers across economic geography and innovation studies. Applicants from diverse international backgrounds can apply, and there is no stated restriction based on race, country, or continent. However, candidates must demonstrate the required academic preparation, quantitative research skills, strong English proficiency, academic writing ability, and genuine interest in the research topic. title: Youth Workers Expert in Strasbourg, France: Freelance Trainer and Facilitator Opportunity for Youth-ID Training of Trainers 2026
summary: Are you an experienced youth worker, trainer, facilitator, or youth practitioner passionate about democratic participation, social inclusion, advocacy, and non-formal education ? ALDA and the Youth-ID project consortium are inviting applications from qualified youth workers experts based in Strasbourg, France , to serve as a freelance trainer and facilitator for an international Training of Trainers (ToT) session in September 2026. The two-day assignment will bring together youth workers from different European countries and will focus on strengthening their practical skills in participatory approaches, inclusive community planning, active citizenship, and youth participation. The training will take place on 15 and 16 September 2026 in Strasbourg, France , with the selected trainer responsible for facilitating practical and experiential learning sessions for a group of 18 youth workers. About the Youth-ID Project The YouthID project is a European initiative funded through the Erasmus+ programme . The project focuses on empowering young people, particularly those from marginalised and underrepresented backgrounds, to become more active participants in their communities. Its broader mission is to provide young people with the knowledge, tools, and confidence needed to: Participate actively in local communities. Engage in decision-making processes. Develop and implement advocacy actions. Contribute to democratic participation. Promote social inclusion. Strengthen their communities. Become active citizens. Build connections with other young people and community actors. A central part of this work involves strengthening the capacity of youth workers and practitioners who support young people. Through innovative educational tools and participatory approaches, YouthID seeks to create long-term impact by strengthening local capacity and encouraging peer learning. About the Training of Trainers Session The Training of Trainers session is designed to bring together committed youth actors from different European countries. The training will focus particularly on developing practical approaches that youth practitioners can use to support: Inclusive community planning. Active citizenship. Democratic participation. Social inclusion. Advocacy. Youth engagement. Participatory learning. The session will take place in Strasbourg , a European capital that provides an appropriate setting for intercultural exchange, European cooperation, and discussions surrounding youth participation and democracy. The selected trainer will therefore play an important role in creating an environment where participants can learn from one another, exchange experiences, and develop practical facilitation skills. Role: Youth Workers Expert, Trainer and Facilitator The selected professional will work as a freelance trainer and facilitator during the two-day Training of Trainers programme. Importantly, the theoretical content and general curriculum have already been developed by the YouthID consortium. Therefore, the trainer will not be expected to design the entire training programme from the beginning. Instead, the primary responsibility will be to deliver the learning sessions effectively and facilitate the group experience . The trainer will work with approximately 18 youth workers from different European countries . Key Responsibilities The selected trainer and facilitator will be responsible for several important areas. 1. Leading Experiential Learning Sessions The trainer will lead learning activities that encourage participants to learn through practical experience rather than relying exclusively on lectures or theoretical presentations. This may include interactive exercises, practical activities, reflection and group-based learning. 2. Facilitating Icebreakers and Group Activities The facilitator will use appropriate icebreakers and group activities to help participants feel comfortable and encourage interaction within an international group. Because participants will come from different European countries and backgrounds, creating a welcoming environment will be an important part of the assignment. 3. Encouraging Dynamic Discussions The trainer will facilitate discussions that encourage participants to: Share experiences. Exchange ideas. Reflect critically. Learn from one another. Explore different perspectives. Develop practical solutions. 4. Creating an Inclusive Learning Environment The selected professional will be expected to create a supportive and inclusive environment where participants feel comfortable contributing. The training should be tailored to an international audience and should encourage participation from all members of the group. 5. Supporting Peer-to-Peer Learning Peer learning is an important component of the programme. The facilitator will encourage participants to share their knowledge and experiences with one another, helping create a collaborative learning environment. 6. Adapting Facilitation Techniques The trainer should be able to adapt their facilitation methods according to the needs and dynamics of the group while still following the objectives of the programme. This requires flexibility, awareness, confidence and strong interpersonal skills. Who Is the Ideal Candidate? The opportunity is aimed at an experienced youth workers expert, trainer or facilitator who has a strong interest in participatory and non-formal education approaches. The ideal candidate should be comfortable working with young adults in an international environment. Required Experience and Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Experience in Youth Training and Facilitation Candidates should have solid experience facilitating: Interactive workshops. Learner-centred sessions. Training activities. Group discussions. Participatory learning sessions. Experience working with young adults is particularly relevant. Strong English Language Skills The entire training will be conducted in English . Therefore, the selected trainer must have a fluent command of English, both spoken and written. Knowledge of Participatory Methods The ideal candidate should have strong expertise in, or enthusiasm for: Participatory methods. Active learning. Non-formal education. Youth participation. Democratic participation. Advocacy. Inclusion. Intersectionality. Organisational Skills The trainer should have excellent organisational skills and demonstrate a professional approach to their work. Positive and Confident Facilitation Style The role requires someone who can confidently facilitate group activities while maintaining a positive and supportive atmosphere. Adaptability is also important because the trainer will work with an international group with different experiences and perspectives. Training Dates and Location The assignment will take place in: Location: Strasbourg, France Dates: 15–16 September 2026 Working hours: 09:00–18:00 on both days This is therefore a two-day freelance training assignment . Payment The selected trainer will receive: €350 total for the two-day assignment. This is the stated fee for the complete two-day training and facilitation assignment. Application Deadline The application deadline is: 31 August 2026 at midnight. Applicants interested in the opportunity should therefore ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated deadline. Why This Opportunity Is Important The assignment provides an opportunity for an experienced youth practitioner to contribute to an international European youth development initiative. The selected trainer will have the opportunity to work with youth workers from different European countries and contribute to discussions and learning around issues such as democratic participation, social inclusion, advocacy and community engagement. The role is particularly relevant for professionals who enjoy facilitating interactive learning and working in multicultural environments. International Exposure The training brings together youth workers from different European countries, creating an international learning environment. This gives the selected facilitator an opportunity to interact with practitioners who bring different experiences, perspectives and approaches to youth work. Contribution to Youth Participation The training directly supports the development of youth workers who work with young people and communities. By strengthening the practical skills of these practitioners, the programme aims to contribute to greater youth participation and social inclusion. Ready-to-Use Training Materials The opportunity indicates that the trainer will benefit from ready-to-use materials developed by the project consortium. This is particularly useful because the trainer s primary responsibility is practical delivery and facilitation rather than developing the entire theoretical curriculum. Professional Networking The selected professional will work within a European network focused on youth participation, democracy and inclusion. This can provide opportunities for professional interaction and knowledge exchange with other youth practitioners and organisations involved in the initiative. Key Areas of Expertise Professionals considering this opportunity should assess their experience in relation to the following areas: Youth work. Youth participation. Democratic participation. Social inclusion. Advocacy. Participatory methods. Intersectionality. Non-formal education. Experiential learning. Workshop facilitation. International youth programmes. Intercultural learning. Community engagement. Candidates do not necessarily need expertise in every area listed above, but the source specifically highlights participatory methods, intersectionality and inclusion, democratic participation and advocacy. Application Process Interested candidates are invited to submit their applications through the designated online application form. The application form is available HERE Applicants should ensure that they provide accurate information demonstrating their relevant experience and suitability for the assignment. Highlight your facilitation experience Explain the types of workshops, trainings or youth programmes you have facilitated, particularly those involving young adults. Demonstrate your participatory approach Show how you use interactive and learner-centred methods rather than relying solely on traditional presentations. Community development. Intercultural learning. Demonstrate international experience If you have worked with multicultural or international groups, make this clear in your application. Show your adaptability Because the role involves working with 18 youth workers from different countries, demonstrate your ability to adjust your facilitation approach according to the needs and dynamics of participants. Taking place on 15 and 16 September 2026 , the assignment will involve facilitating practical learning for 18 youth workers from across Europe. The selected trainer will use interactive methods, encourage peer learning, support inclusive participation and adapt facilitation techniques to the needs of an international group. With a €350 fee for the two-day assignment , ready-to-use programme materials and the opportunity to contribute to an Erasmus+ youth initiative, the role is particularly suited to professionals with strong facilitation and non-formal education experience. title: Duke University Global Health Innovation and Policy Faculty Position 2026: Associate Professor or Professor Opportunity in the United States
summary: Duke University is inviting applications for a senior faculty position in Global Health Innovation and Policy at the Duke Global Health Institute (DGHI) in Durham, North Carolina, United States. The position is being jointly conducted by the Duke Global Health Institute, Duke-Margolis Institute for Health Policy, and Duke Global Health Innovation Center . Duke is seeking an experienced professional with significant expertise in global health innovation, health policy, health financing, or closely related areas to strengthen research, policy and leadership activities at Duke. The successful candidate will be appointed at the Associate Professor or Professor level and will have opportunities to contribute to research, policy engagement, teaching, mentorship, partnership development, external funding, and leadership within the Duke Global Health Innovation Center and the wider university. Duke University Global Health Faculty Position: Key Details This is a senior-level academic and professional opportunity for an established global health expert with a strong record of research, external funding, publications, stakeholder engagement and leadership. The main details of the position include: Institution: Duke University Institute: Duke Global Health Institute Position title: Faculty Position in Global Health Innovation and Policy Academic level: Associate Professor or Professor Position type: Non-tenure-track faculty Location: Durham, North Carolina, United States Primary appointment: Duke Global Health Institute Track: Research or practice track Appointment: Full-time, 9- or 12-month appointment Initial appointment: Three years Reappointment: Possible at the conclusion of the initial three-year term Position ID: Duke-DGHI-FACULTY [#32464] Subject area: Global Health The position is intended for a senior individual who can combine academic excellence with practical impact in global health innovation and policy. What Is Duke Looking For? Duke is looking for a candidate with significant expertise and experience in one or more of the following areas: Global health innovation Health policy Health financing Policy analysis Operational research Research on health innovation Development and introduction of health innovations Scaling health innovations in low-resource settings Policy engagement Global health systems The institution is particularly interested in professionals who have demonstrated the ability to move beyond research alone and translate knowledge into practical solutions that can be implemented in real-world settings. Duke describes innovation broadly. It may involve something entirely new or something that has been newly adapted to a particular local context and produces meaningful impact. Such innovation could take the form of: A product A service A programme An enterprise An applied solution The university emphasizes that successful innovation should be effective, scalable, sustainable and equitable . Experience in Low-Resource and Global Settings Although the position allows flexibility regarding specific topics, populations and contexts, Duke has a particular interest in candidates who have worked on health innovation in low-resource contexts globally . Relevant experience may include leading: Research on health innovations Policy analysis Operational research Development of health innovations Introduction of health innovations Scale-up of health innovations Policy engagement activities Experience across different low-resource settings is particularly relevant because the successful candidate will be expected to understand how innovations can be adapted to different environments rather than assuming that one solution will work identically everywhere. Duke Welcomes Non-Traditional Career Paths An important feature of this opportunity is Duke s openness to candidates who have followed non-traditional professional paths. The position specifically welcomes team-science-oriented professionals who have moved between different sectors during their careers. Examples include professionals with experience across: Universities and academic institutions Government Multilateral organizations Social enterprises Implementation organizations Practitioner settings This means candidates do not necessarily need to have followed a purely academic career trajectory if they can demonstrate strong relevant expertise, leadership, research, policy and practical experience. Leadership and Management Responsibilities Duke is also seeking an individual with substantial management and leadership experience . The successful candidate could serve in a faculty leadership capacity at the Duke Global Health Innovation Center . Leadership responsibilities may include: Managing people Managing budgets Managing organizations or programmes Representing the Center externally Engaging funders Working with governments Engaging implementation partners Supporting business development Developing partnerships Advancing funded programmes Traveling domestically and internationally when necessary The position therefore goes beyond traditional teaching and research responsibilities. It is designed for a senior professional who can help build partnerships, attract resources, manage programmes and represent Duke in global health innovation activities. Research, Policy and Practical Impact One of the central features of the position is the connection between research, policy and practical implementation. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to research and policy efforts while also demonstrating an understanding of how evidence can influence real-world health systems and programmes. This makes the position particularly relevant to professionals who can demonstrate that their work has moved from academic research into areas such as: Government policy Health programme implementation Innovation scale-up Public-sector decision-making Stakeholder engagement Health financing Health-system improvement Partnerships with implementation organizations Duke is looking for someone who can understand both the academic and practical dimensions of global health innovation. External Funding Experience A significant record of extramural funding is one of the required qualifications for the position. Duke is particularly interested in applicants who have obtained funding from diverse sources, including: Governments Foundations Industry The position s long-term salary support will come predominantly from extramural grant funding, although additional internal sources may contribute over time through activities such as teaching and administrative responsibilities. Because of this funding model, competitive candidates must be able to demonstrate their ability to communicate the value of their work and develop funded programmes that are sustainable and add value to the Duke Global Health Innovation Center s portfolio. Duke Global Health Institute and Duke-Margolis will support the successful faculty member in transitioning into the institution and developing successful programmes. Teaching and Mentorship Opportunities The position also places considerable importance on teaching and mentorship . Duke is seeking an applicant who is passionate about mentoring students and developing the next generation of global health professionals alongside their research and policy activities. The successful faculty member may mentor: Undergraduate students Global Health majors Graduate students in the Master of Science in Global Health programme Graduate students in other Duke programmes Doctoral students across the university Medical school doctoral students Postdoctoral scholars Junior faculty The faculty member may also participate in students ongoing research and studies. In addition, the successful candidate could develop new courses related to: Global health systems Innovation Health policy Health financing They may also teach existing courses in these areas. Appointment Structure and Work Location This is a full-time 9- or 12-month appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor. The primary appointment will be within the Duke Global Health Institute, and the position will be a regular-rank non-tenure-track appointment in either the research or practice track. The initial appointment is for three years , with eligibility for reappointment at the end of that period. Rank and salary will be determined based on the successful candidate s qualifications and experience. There is also potential for a joint appointment in another department or school at Duke University. Because the role involves extensive collaboration, teaching, mentoring and partnership responsibilities, candidates are expected to be able to work in the United States and maintain regular presence in Durham, North Carolina. Relocation or substantial on-campus engagement is expected. About the Duke Global Health Institute The Duke Global Health Institute (DGHI) was established in 2006 as a university-wide institute bringing together faculty from across Duke. Its vision is focused on achieving health equity for vulnerable populations around the world. The institute works across several areas, including: Preparing global health leaders through interdisciplinary education. Conducting research into major global health challenges. Designing policies. Developing evidence-based interventions. Partnering with international and local organizations. Supporting locally grounded and collaborative projects. Developing innovative solutions to global health challenges. The DGHI community includes staff, primary and secondary faculty, affiliate faculty and adjunct faculty. The institute also emphasizes values including humility, compassion, respect, cultural sensitivity, collaboration, diversity, inclusion and commitment to impact. Duke-Margolis Institute for Health Policy The position is also connected to the Robert J. Margolis, MD, Institute for Health Policy at Duke University , commonly referred to as Duke-Margolis. Duke-Margolis brings together expertise from the Washington, DC policy community, Duke University and Duke Health. Practical experience applying global health innovation in real-world settings. Policy expertise and experience engaging policymakers. External funding success from governments, foundations, industry or other sources. Leadership experience involving people, budgets and organizations. Partnership-building skills with governments, funders and implementation organizations. The position is therefore intended for an established professional rather than an early-career applicant. title: European Union Press and Information Officer Job in Switzerland 2026: Salary, Requirements, Responsibilities and How to Apply
summary: The European Union Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein has announced a new employment opportunity for an experienced communications, media, public relations or international affairs professional. The position is for a Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) within the Political, Press and Information Section of the EU Delegation in Bern, Switzerland. This opportunity is particularly relevant for professionals with substantial experience in media relations, strategic communication, digital communications, public diplomacy, journalism, public relations and event management who also have strong knowledge of German, French and English. The position is offered as a Local Agent Group I role under a fixed-term employment contract of two years, with the possibility of renewal subject to budgetary availability and operational considerations. The successful applicant is expected to begin work on 1 March 2027 . Press and Information Officer Job Opportunity at the EU Delegation The European Union is an economic and political partnership made up of 27 European countries and plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development assistance and cooperation with global organizations. Outside the European Union, it is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations known as EU Delegations. These Delegations perform functions comparable in some respects to embassies and represent the EU in relations with governments and other stakeholders. The EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein is based in Bern, Switzerland . It works closely with the embassies and consulates of the 27 EU Member States and represents the European Union in dealings with the Swiss government on matters falling within the EU s responsibilities. The advertised Press and Information Officer will become part of the Delegation s Political, Press and Information Section. The role combines press relations, public diplomacy, social media, digital communication, event management, strategic communication and a smaller policy component. Position Details The position provides an opportunity to work directly within a diplomatic environment and contribute to the communication and public diplomacy activities of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Key details include: Position: Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) Group: Local Agent Group I Section: Political, Press and Information Section Location: EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein, Bern, Switzerland Contract: Fixed-term employment contract Contract duration: Two years Renewal: Possible, subject to budgetary availability and operational considerations Probationary period: Three months Expected start date: 1 March 2027 Working arrangement: Full time Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday Additional requirements: Occasional evening and weekend work and travel for work missions The successful candidate will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Political, Press and Information Section. The role involves providing expertise and assistance in social media, digital communication and public relations. What Will the Press and Information Officer Do? The Press and Information Officer will have a central role in representing and communicating the activities, policies and values of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The successful applicant will act as the EU Delegation s spokesperson and will advise the Ambassador on communication-related matters. The position will also serve as a key point of contact between the Delegation and journalists and media organizations. The officer will contribute significantly to the Delegation s overall press, communication and visibility strategy while managing its digital presence and developing content for social media, websites and video platforms. Another major component of the position is public diplomacy. This includes organizing events, engaging stakeholders and developing outreach activities designed to strengthen awareness and understanding of the EU, its activities and its values. Main Duties and Responsibilities Approximately 85% of the position s time will be dedicated to press, communication and public diplomacy, while approximately 15% will be dedicated to policy-related work. 1. Press, Communication and Public Diplomacy The largest part of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy. Public Relations and Media The Press and Information Officer will be responsible for: Maintaining and developing professional relationships with local and international journalists. Working with media organizations and government press agencies. Preparing and distributing press releases, press reviews and articles for publication. Preparing interviews and speeches for the Head of Delegation. Developing and implementing public diplomacy strategies designed to improve perceptions and understanding of the EU in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Preparing speeches, briefings and other information materials for the media. Monitoring local and European media. Preparing media reports. Managing requests from journalists and coordinating responses with appropriate internal stakeholders. Organizing media coverage during official missions and events. Collaborating with EU Headquarters services and strategic communications task forces to maintain consistent messaging and communication strategies. This means the successful applicant will need to be comfortable working in a fast-paced media environment where accuracy, speed, diplomacy and strong judgment are essential. 2. Social Media and Digital Communication Digital communication is another major component of the role. The officer will lead the Delegation s digital and social media strategy and will be responsible for managing and producing content for relevant social media platforms and the Delegation s website. Responsibilities include: Developing informative, engaging and accurate digital content. Creating and implementing digital communication plans. Developing social media campaigns. Managing cross-posting activities. Supporting livestreaming and event coverage. Monitoring social media analytics and performance. Recommending improvements to strengthen digital communication. Improving the Delegation s online visibility. Coordinating digital campaigns with external service providers. Candidates therefore need more than conventional writing or journalism skills. The position requires practical understanding of modern digital communications, social media strategy, analytics, web publishing and multimedia communication. 3. Event Management and Public Outreach The successful applicant will also lead or coordinate public diplomacy and outreach activities. This includes: Preparing public diplomacy events. Organizing public outreach activities. Supporting high-level visits and site visits. Working on events involving the Ambassador and other EU officials. Coordinating with cultural, academic and diplomatic partners. Strengthening the impact of public diplomacy activities. Organizing cultural and visibility events that promote EU values and activities. This aspect of the position makes event management and stakeholder engagement important areas of expertise. 4. Strategic Support and Administration The Press and Information Officer will also: Support the preparation of reports and strategic documents. Assist with internal and external communication plans. Support planning and management of the Delegation s press and information budget. Assist with procurement and contract management. Policy Responsibilities Although the majority of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy, approximately 15% of the officer s time will be dedicated to policy. The policy component includes monitoring, policy analysis and reporting concerning EU-Switzerland cooperation in EU programmes , including areas such as: Erasmus+ Research Innovation Science Culture Candidates who understand European affairs, EU institutions and EU-Switzerland relations may therefore have an advantage when demonstrating their suitability for the position. Salary and Benefits The vacancy states that the base salary will depend on the candidate s relevant and verified employment experience, with the salary typically starting from CHF 10,343 . The position also comes with a competitive benefits package, subject to applicable conditions. The stated benefits include: Personal leave days Public holidays A retirement savings plan Health insurance, including accident insurance Partial reimbursement of LAMal-related costs The expected start date for the successful candidate is 1 March 2027 . Who Can Apply? Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before submitting an application because the vacancy specifically states that applicants must verify that they satisfy all conditions. The position requires a combination of academic qualifications, professional experience, language proficiency and legal authorization to live and work in Switzerland. Minimum Educational Requirement Applicants must hold a university degree in a field relevant to the position . Relevant fields include: Political science Communication International relations Media Journalism Public relations Related fields Professional Experience Applicants must have at least five years of professional experience in a relevant field . Relevant experience may include: Media Online publishing Public relations Communication Events Similar professional areas The vacancy specifies that this professional experience must have been obtained after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained . Language Requirements One of the most important requirements is language proficiency. Applicants must have excellent C1-level knowledge of German, French and English . This is particularly important because the role involves communication with journalists, government stakeholders, diplomatic partners, EU institutions and the wider public. Right to Work in Switzerland Applicants must have the right to reside and work in Switzerland , subject to approval by the competent authorities where applicable. This requirement is especially important for international applicants. The vacancy does not state that the position is universally open to candidates who would require unrestricted sponsorship or authorization to work in Switzerland. Additional Qualifications That Can Strengthen an Application The vacancy also identifies assets and selection criteria that may help candidates earn points during the selection process. These include: A postgraduate degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or a related field. Experience working in a diplomatic mission. Experience working for a development agency. Experience in a multicultural international environment. Experience working with European Union policies and procedures. These are presented as assets rather than the basic minimum requirements, meaning candidates should distinguish carefully between mandatory eligibility conditions and additional experience that can strengthen their application. Skills Required for the Position The successful candidate should have a broad combination of strategic communication, digital, analytical, writing and interpersonal skills. Important skills include: Translating complicated policy issues into language suitable for traditional and social media. Developing communication strategies and plans. Maintaining a good professional network within Swiss media. Understanding local and European cultural interaction. Understanding EU institutions, history and priorities. Understanding EU-Switzerland relations. Strong knowledge of digital media and communication techniques. Knowledge of graphic and layout editing and design tools. Knowledge of web publication tools. Excellent writing skills. Ability to prepare concise and clear notes. Ability to communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing. This combination demonstrates that the role is designed for an experienced communications professional who can move comfortably between strategic planning, media engagement, digital production, public speaking and policy communication. Personal and Behavioral Qualities Beyond academic and professional qualifications, the EU Delegation is looking for someone who can operate effectively in a demanding diplomatic environment. The vacancy highlights the following qualities: Ability to multitask. Ability to work under time pressure. Proactive approach to work. Ability to take appropriate action without constant prompting. Flexibility when responding to new requests. Ability to build and maintain professional relationships. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural team. Strong interpersonal skills. Ability to prioritize tasks. Initiative and good workload organization. Ability to meet deadlines. Confidence speaking before large audiences. Ability to lead or introduce public events. Service-oriented mindset. Professional attitude and appearance. Willingness to learn and develop new competencies. High levels of integrity, confidentiality and responsibility. Working Environment The Press and Information Officer position is a full-time role involving 37.5 hours per week from Monday to Friday . However, candidates should be prepared for occasional atypical working hours, including evenings and weekends. The position also involves travel for work missions. The job is primarily office-based and does not involve specific or unusual physical requirements. The officer will work closely with colleagues within the Political, Press and Information Section and other parts of the organization. The role also requires regular cooperation with: EU Headquarters Cultural partners Academic partners Diplomatic partners External service providers Journalists and media organizations Other relevant stakeholders How to Apply for the EU Press and Information Officer Position Eligible candidates must prepare and submit the required application documents by email. The application must include: 1. Cover Letter Applicants must submit a signed cover letter . The cover letter should demonstrate the candidate s suitability for the position and should clearly connect their professional experience and qualifications to the responsibilities described in the vacancy. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must also submit a Curriculum Vitæ . The CV must include, at minimum: Exact job titles Employers names Detailed descriptions of tasks and responsibilities The vacancy specifically requests that applicants use one of the Europass CV templates . follow templates here: https://europass.europa.eu/en Application Email The completed application should be sent to: eeasjobs-078@eeas.europa.eu Applicants must use the following re ference in the email subject: Ref: 157570 – Press and Information Officer Applications may be submitted in English or French . Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications is: 18 September 2026 at 24:00 CET. Applicants should ensure that their complete application reaches the Delegation before the stated deadline. The vacancy explicitly gives this deadline in both its announcement and application instructions. Because the application requires multiple documents and the CV must contain detailed employment information, candidates should avoid waiting until the final day to prepare and submit their applications. Important Application Warning The vacancy contains an important caution for applicants. Candidates are responsible for verifying that they meet all applicable conditions . The application instructions indicate that applicants must mark the relevant boxes relating to each document or application condition. The absence of a required condition or document can result in the rejection of the application. Applicants should therefore review the requirements carefully before submitting their documents rather than assuming that meeting some of the criteria will be sufficient. Selection Process After the application deadline, eligible applications will be considered by a Selection Committee established for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, the selection process may involve several stages. These may include: Eligibility screening of submitted applications. Shortlisting based on information provided in the CV and cover letter. Practical testing , depending on the selection process. Interviews . Final interview stage for the strongest candidates. The vacancy states that the three best candidates will be invited to the final interview . If the first two candidates have an equivalent ranking after the interviews, a written test will be organized. Only candidates who progress through each successive stage will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not provide additional information about or discuss the selection procedure. Candidates are also instructed not to contact members of the Selection Committee during the recruitment process. Questions and comments should instead be directed to the Delegation s Administration. Medical Check The successful candidate will be required to undergo a medical check to assess their fitness to perform the duties associated with the position. Equal Opportunities The European Union states that it is committed to equal opportunities for employees and applicants. Its stated approach includes: Promoting gender equality. Preventing discrimination on any grounds. Maintaining zero tolerance for harassment. Welcoming qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. Promoting a workplace where employees are respected. Supporting employees in developing their full potential. Candidates with disabilities who are pre-selected are invited to contact the Delegation so that appropriate assistance and accommodations can be considered to ensure equal opportunities during the recruitment process. Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for Communications Professionals This position offers an opportunity to work within a European Union diplomatic representation and contribute to the way the EU communicates with the public, media, government stakeholders and partner organizations in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The role combines several professional areas that are increasingly interconnected in modern international communications, including: Strategic communications Journalism and media relations Public relations Social media management Digital communications Public diplomacy Event management Stakeholder engagement Policy communication International relations EU affairs For professionals who already have significant experience in these areas, the position could provide exposure to high-level diplomatic communication, European policy issues and international stakeholder engagement. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Although the vacancy sets out the formal requirements, candidates can improve the clarity and relevance of their application by ensuring that their documents directly demonstrate how their experience corresponds to the position. Tip 1: Highlight Relevant Professional Experience Because five years of relevant professional experience is a minimum requirement, candidates should clearly demonstrate this experience in their CV. Rather than simply listing job titles, applicants should provide detailed descriptions of their responsibilities, as specifically requested in the vacancy. Tip 2: Demonstrate Communication Expertise The position is heavily focused on press, communication and public diplomacy, accounting for approximately 85% of the role. Applicants should therefore make relevant experience in areas such as media relations, journalism, public relations, digital communications, social media campaigns, public outreach and event management easy to identify. Tip 3: Make Language Proficiency Clear German, French and English are all specifically required at C1 level. Applicants should make their language abilities clear and easy for the Selection Committee to verify. Tip 4: Connect Experience to EU and International Affairs Experience with EU policies and procedures, diplomatic missions, development agencies or multicultural international environments is identified as an asset. Candidates who possess this experience should make it prominent in their application. Tip 5: Use the Required CV Format The vacancy specifically requests a CV using a Europass template . Candidates should therefore follow the stated application instructions rather than submitting an unrelated CV format. Tip 6: Check Every Requirement Before Submission The Delegation explicitly warns that missing conditions or documents can result in rejection. Candidates should use the vacancy requirements as a checklist and confirm that all requested documents and eligibility conditions have been addressed before submitting their application. The opportunity is aimed at experienced professional candidates who meet the stated requirements. The key qualifying profile is: A university degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or a related field. At least five years of relevant professional experience obtained after the qualification required for the post. C1-level knowledge of German, French and English. The right to reside and work in Switzerland, subject to applicable approval requirements. Candidates with postgraduate qualifications, diplomatic or development-sector experience, multicultural international experience, or experience with EU policies and procedures may have additional advantages during selection. Nationality/region: The vacancy does not state a specific nationality, race or continent restriction. Instead, it expressly requires applicants to have the right to reside and work in Switzerland . Therefore, prospective applicants should assess their legal eligibility to work in Switzerland rather than assuming that nationality alone determines eligibility. Conclusion The Press and Information Officer vacancy at the European Union Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein is a substantial professional opportunity for an experienced communications, media, public relations, journalism, digital communications or international affairs specialist. The role combines press relations, strategic communication, social media, digital content, public diplomacy, event management, stakeholder engagement and policy analysis. With a stated base salary typically starting from CHF 10,343 , a two-year fixed-term contract, a competitive benefits package and an expected start date of 1 March 2027 , the position offers the opportunity to work in an international diplomatic environment in Bern. Applicants should pay particular attention to the mandatory requirements, especially the university degree, minimum five years of relevant professional experience, C1-level German, French and English, and the right to reside and work in Switzerland.
